answers.answer:
RAG‑Token treats each output token as potentially coming from a different retrieved document.  
For every token the model draws a latent document \(z\) from the top‑\(k\) retrieved set, generates a distribution for that token conditioned on \(z\), and then marginalises over all \(z\) before moving to the next token. This lets the generator mix information from several documents token‑by‑token.  
[rag‑knowledge‑intensive‑nlp.pdf — Page 4]

RAG‑Sequence, on the other hand, conditions the entire sequence on a single latent document.  
It runs beam search separately for each retrieved document, scores each full‑sequence hypothesis with the generator conditioned on that document, and then marginalises over the documents after the whole sequence has been generated. Thus the model uses one document per hypothesis rather than one per token.  
[rag‑knowledge‑intensive‑nlp.pdf — Page 4]
